about: Every 'chain checks' clause of every story in M1-STORIES.md, split into atomic claims and reconciled with the Lean. class: guard (the Lean decides it), omission (the Lean does not model it; the simulator says so), overrule (the Lean decides differently; the simulator follows the Lean). A guard or overrule row is one claim of one kind — guard (a hypothesis the transition requires), refusal (the clause states a refusal), payment (a flow field pays it), post-state (the resulting state, optionally 'updates': the only datum fields the post-state sets), no-guard (the constructor has no hypothesis), verdict (a conjunct of consumableState) — and names the Lean declaration (decl: a Step constructor, consumableState, SysStep.register, Trace.cons or a theorem), the hypothesis for a guard or refusal (hyp), the exact text that entails the claim (text), and exactly one semantic tie: reason (a refusal name, which the core's LEAN_GUARDS binds to the constructor and binder that refuse it; a refusal claim also needs a step of its story refused for it), verdict (bound to its conjunct), or match (a step of the story's own scenario, whose constructor is derived from the record; a payment claim's step must pay through the named field; an untouched-except claim's step must change only the listed fields). The scenario gate parses each constructor into its hypotheses, flow record and post-state and requires the text inside the part the kind names; it fails on an unclassified fragment, a clause absent from its story, a text outside its part, a tie the declaration does not decide, and a Step guard hypothesis no refusal name claims.

clauses.clause: the inception parses and self-addresses
clauses.note: Step.register carries no inception and no validation predicate; the registrant's bytes are not modelled. The Env has no predicate for it either.

clauses.clause: the AID is absent from the registry
and is inserted
clauses.note: Sys.set moves the leaf with the state (State.leaf); SysStep.other leaves the registry alone for rotate, poison, freeze and top-up (T8_edges_leave_the_leaf).

clauses.clause: this is the only way the token can ever be minted
clauses.note: registration is the only SysStep that touches the registry, and it needs the AID absent from it; every non-absent AID is registered (T8_present_implies_registered), so a second minting is refused for the rest of the AID's life.

clauses.clause: both bonds are present
clauses.note: the registration flow brings exactly D and B; a transaction bringing less is not a Step at all.

clauses.clause: signatures at the current threshold over the rotation bytes
clauses.note: one predicate stands for the three cryptographic checks of the advance (Env.rotationTo doc); the same hev guards every rotate constructor and the freeze.

clauses.clause: revealed keys match the pre-committed digests at the next threshold
receipts from at least `toad` of the new witness set
sequence strictly greater
Then it pays `P` from the pool to Hal
clauses.text: hunter := some { addr := payee, pool := p.P }
clauses.note: paid when the pool covers P (hpay : p.P ≤ l.pool); otherwise the rotation lands unpaid (Step.rotateKeepUnpaid, hnopay): payment is never a gate.

clauses.clause: exactly the advance predicate on the presented rotation
that the pool is below `P`
that the checkpoint is not poisoned
already unconsumable
nothing to freeze
clauses.note: the rationale of the modelling assumption stated on Step.freeze's doc comment (no freeze from a poisoned state); the Lean has the guard hclean, not the reason for it.

clauses.clause: Then it pays `B` to Hal
clauses.text: hunter := some { addr := payee, b := p.B }
clauses.note: the freeze also needs the bond present (hb : l.frozen = false; refusal freeze-bond-missing), which the story states only as its 'after'.

clauses.clause: and leaves the datum untouched
clauses.note: Live is the datum plus the value held; the freeze sets only the frozen bit (the freeze bond leaves as value) and leaves sn, epoch, poisoned, bornAt, refundTo and pool as they were — the old keys stay.

clauses.clause: the advance predicate
clauses.note: story 4's deposit lands with the pool short (hnopay), the unpaid constructor; Step.rotateDepositPaid carries the same guards.

clauses.clause: the new keys' signature on the deposit
then the freeze bond is back on the output
clauses.note: the flow brings p.B − bHeld: B when frozen, nothing when the bond is held (a deposit on full bonds is a keep, T5_deposit_on_full_is_keep).

clauses.clause: nothing else changes and juvenility is not restarted
clauses.note: D-040: the deposit is the unfreeze, not a bonding; bornAt is untouched (slice 2 reset it).

clauses.clause: the advance predicate
clauses.note: a close is a witnessed rotation (D-036); Step.closeUnpaid carries the same guards.

clauses.clause: the new keys' signature on the close naming the payee and the refund address
clauses.note: one message carries the close, its payee and the optional new address (D-038, D-039).

clauses.clause: a copied reap with another payee or address is refused
clauses.note: D-039, the registry's Q-R6: the payee is inside the signed message, so a copy with the payee rewritten presents a message the keys never signed (T16_copied_reap_refused).

clauses.clause: then it pays the premium to the payee
clauses.text: hunter := some { addr := payee, pool := p.P }
clauses.note: paid when the pool covers P (hpay); otherwise the reap lands unpaid (Step.closeUnpaid, hnopay): payment is never a gate.

clauses.clause: and everything else to the refund address
clauses.text: refund := some { addr := refund'.getD l.refundTo, dreg := p.D, b := l.bHeld p, pool := l.pool - p.P }

clauses.clause: burns the token
clauses.note: the post-state is not a present checkpoint: no UTxO (T8_utxo_iff_active).

clauses.clause: and parks the leaf with the hash of the checkpoint the rotation reached
clauses.note: the hash is the key state the closing rotation reached (T16_parked_hash_is_the_closed_checkpoints), not the datum it spent: a revival must rotate from it, so the close's own rotation cannot revive (T1_close_rotation_cannot_revive).

clauses.clause: the leaf is parked
clauses.note: the registry's presence proof; for one AID the state guard refuses first (reopen-needs-parked), the leaf guard is the system-level reason the gate's generator exercises.

clauses.clause: a witnessed rotation from exactly the parked key state
clauses.note: only the holder of the next keys of the parked key state can produce it: a thief of the current keys cannot revive (T4_current_key_thief_cannot_revive).

clauses.clause: strictly later than the parked sequence
fresh bonds and a first pool come in
clauses.text: dregIn := p.D, bIn := p.B, poolIn := pool0

clauses.clause: the checkpoint is born now at the next epoch
clauses.text: ⟨sn', h.epoch + 1, false, false, now, refund, pool0⟩
clauses.note: juvenile for W slots (T10_reopen_is_juvenile), unfrozen, unpoisoned, with the refund address whoever pays chose.

clauses.clause: signatures at the current threshold
one stolen member key of a multisig cannot poison
clauses.note: the threshold itself is inside Env.quorum; a single member key is not modelled.

clauses.clause: that the epoch is not already poisoned
the signature over the new address at the new threshold by the keys the rotation reveals
A relayer submitting her public rotation without that signature leaves the address unchanged
clauses.note: a rotation that names an address the new keys did not sign in the intent message is refused whole (hauth fails), not landed with the old address; a rotation naming no address needs no signature and keeps it. Story 8's scenario plays both (D-032, D-038).

clauses.clause: the second rotation is at the tip's sequence
reveals the same keys the tip holds
clauses.note: one predicate stands for the whole duplicity check (Env.duplicityAt doc).

clauses.clause: is signed at the current threshold
carries receipts from at least `toad` of the tip's witnesses
and differs from the accepted one
No history needed: the revealed keys are the current keys
clauses.note: the model has no key material; the epoch counter stands for the current keys, and duplicityAt is asked at (epoch, sn) only.

clauses.clause: a witnessed rotation by the next keys, poisoned or not
clauses.note: no poison guard on either close constructor (D-036): Mallory with the current keys is refused for the missing rotation, and Alice's reap lands from the poisoned state.

clauses.clause: the signed close naming the payee
then it pays the premium to the payee
clauses.text: hunter := some { addr := payee, pool := p.P }

clauses.clause: and everything else to the refund address
clauses.text: refund := some { addr := refund'.getD l.refundTo, dreg := p.D, b := l.bHeld p, pool := l.pool - p.P }

clauses.clause: the closer never chooses where the bonds go
clauses.note: the refund address is the datum's unless the new keys signed a new one in the same message (D-032, D-038); a thief with the next keys who reaps still pays Alice's address (story 10's fork).

clauses.clause: present
the freeze bond held
clauses.note: the conviction bond is always held by a present checkpoint (D-040), so it is no conjunct.

clauses.clause: not poisoned
born at least `W` slots ago
the signature on the payment satisfies the current threshold
clauses.note: the consumer's own threshold check on its transaction is outside this machine (consumableState doc).

clauses.clause: Later, when validity ships: within `valid_until`
clauses.note: validity (D-027, A11) is reserved in the datum and not modelled (Checkpoint.lean module doc).

clauses.clause: on: absent
clauses.note: every non-present state is False; each present failure names its conjunct (story 11's scenario walks all six).

clauses.clause: frozen
poisoned
juvenile
parked
clauses.note: no UTxO to read: the leaf holds the hash and nothing else (D-040).

clauses.clause: convicted
the checkpoint is juvenile for `W` slots
anyone can advance it onward with Alice's later public rotations
clauses.note: the submitter is not modelled. Action.actor derives the authorizer from the action and a rotation's is nextKeys — Alice's rotation authorizes itself; nothing in Step or SysStep names who carries the transaction. Scenario 12 plays Hal landing Alice's later rotation, which the Lean admits because the evidence (hev) holds, not because 'anyone' is a rule of the machine. Campaign 1 anchored this to `| .register .. => .anyone`, the actor of a registration: an over-attribution.

clauses.clause: the moment that happens, Mallory's bonds answer to Alice's keys (story 8)
clauses.note: the bonds answer to whoever can move the refund address: after Alice's rotation only her new keys can sign a new one in the intent message (hauth, D-038), and the reap pays there (Step.closePaid / Step.closeUnpaid), never to the closer.

clauses.clause: It can happen once per AID, ever
clauses.note: for one AID the state guard (present / parked / convicted) refuses first (already-present, as scenario 12 plays it); the leaf guard is the system-level reason, exercised by the gate's multi-AID generator.

clauses.clause: add value to the pool
the datum is untouched
clauses.note: only the pool (value) moves; sn, epoch, poisoned, frozen, bornAt and refundTo stay — juvenility is not restarted.

clauses.clause: no signature
clauses.note: the constructor has no guard hypothesis: no evidence, no signature.

clauses.clause: Both see the rotation
clauses.note: hunters, watchers and timing are not modelled; evidence is a table.

clauses.clause: If the pool covers `P`
the first advance wins and is paid
clauses.text: hunter := some { addr := payee, pool := p.P }
clauses.note: no UTxO in the model: 'first' is whichever rotation the machine sees first; it lands paid.

clauses.clause: the second fails on the spent input
clauses.note: no UTxO in the model: the second advance fails because the state moved and its evidence no longer matches (no-witnessed-rotation).

clauses.clause: If it does not
the first freeze wins `B`
clauses.text: hunter := some { addr := payee, b := p.B }

clauses.clause: the second finds nothing to take
and no rotation is missing
clauses.note: consumableState has no predicate over rotations the checkpoint has not seen: the state-side conjuncts read the datum only. A missing rotation is what a freeze (story 3) makes visible, not what the consumer sees. Campaign 1 anchored this to the juvenility conjunct: an over-attribution.

clauses.clause: Nothing on chain says she is gone
clauses.note: no age, no liveness signal in the datum; consumableState reads bornAt only for juvenility.

clauses.clause: a validity Alice renews by re-signing with her current keys
clauses.note: D-027 direction, not ruled; the fields are reserved in the datum and absent from the model (Checkpoint.lean module doc).

clauses.clause: no next-key reveal
clauses.note: D-027 direction; not in the model.

clauses.clause: if it lapses, only a rotation brings the checkpoint back
clauses.note: D-027 direction; not in the model.

clauses.clause: The fields are reserved in the datum now
clauses.note: reserved fields are not in Live.

clauses.clause: her checkpoint stays consumable as long as it is bonded
clauses.note: consumableState has no upper bound on age; bonded means a present checkpoint (the conviction bond is always held) with the freeze bond held (next row).

clauses.clause: her checkpoint stays consumable as long as it is bonded
